sections.h2: Selling a house in Bowling Green
sections.html:
Warren County's seat is a college-and-factory city on the Barren River, third in Kentucky after Louisville and Lexington. The July 2025 estimate is 78,505 people, up 8.6 percent from 2020. Interstate 65 runs through town between Louisville and Nashville, Interstate 165 heads north to Owensboro, and US 31W, US 231 and US 68/KY 80 cross it as well.

Only 36.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied, so this is a renter's city, and a house here is often sold to an investor or landlord as readily as to a family. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $241,900. Median gross rent is $998 a month, and median owner costs are $1,447 with a mortgage and $553 without. The 2020 census counted 31,797 housing units, with 11.4 percent vacant and a rental vacancy rate of 11.5 percent. With rental vacancy above 11 percent, a house listed as a rental can sit empty between leases, which is worth weighing if you own one.

sections.h2: City and school tax rates by location
sections.html:
Two collectors send bills here. The city's Treasury office bills for the city and for the Bowling Green Independent School System, and the Warren County Sheriff sends the county bill. The city mails roughly 23,000 bills each October, due in full by December 31. Unpaid city taxes can face a foreclosure action filed six months after the due date. The rates below are per $100.

Real estate tax rates per $100 by location, City of Bowling Green Finance Department
Where the house isTotal real estate rate
City proper (city limits and city schools)1.3625
Annex (city limits, county schools)1.0455
Outside city limits (county schools)0.8425

City proper adds a 0.2030 city rate and an 0.8420 city school rate to the county's 0.2145 and the state's 0.1030. Check the Finance page for the rate in force when you sell.

sections.h2: Which school district is a house in?
sections.html: The answer depends on the street. Bowling Green Independent serves the inner city, and Warren County Public Schools has the outlying sections. An "annex" of homes inside city limits attends county schools, and the school tax rate differs between the two. Tell buyers which district applies, since it moves the tax figure.

sections.h2: Paying the county bill and closing
sections.html:
The Warren County Sheriff prefers a check or money order mailed to P.O. Box 807, Bowling Green, KY 42102, or delivered to 1347 KY-185, Suite 1. The office answers at (270) 842-1633. Online card payments carry a $1.50 fee up to $60 and 2.49 percent above that. Partial payments are not accepted on a current-year bill.

  • 2 percent discount from October 1 through November 1, face value from November 2 through December 31, a 5 percent penalty in January and 21 percent from February 1 through April 15.
  • Kentucky law issues the bill in the name of the January 1 owner. If you sold, forward the bill to the buyer.
  • A closing agent or attorney usually prorates the year between buyer and seller, but the sheriff needs the full bill paid by one or both of them.

For a delinquent prior year, call the Warren County Clerk at (270) 842-9416 for the payoff.

Owners 65 or older, and owners who are totally disabled, can apply for the homestead and disability exemptions at the PVA, (270) 843-3268. Apply before you list if you qualify, because a buyer has to file again on their own.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax bills
sections.html: After April 15 an unpaid bill becomes a certificate of delinquency, recorded as a lien under KRS 134.122, and the County Attorney reports 12 percent annual interest under KRS 134.125. If the certificate stays unpaid 90 days, third-party purchasers may buy it. A certificate cannot be sold while the owner has a payment agreement with the County Attorney, whose office offers plans running 4 to 8 months at (270) 782-2760. If a purchaser already bought the certificate, you deal with that purchaser instead. The clerk's sale takes place each summer at 429 E 10th Ave, Suite 100.

The Building and Inspection Division at 707 E Main Ave, reachable at 270-393-3615 or 270-393-3676 on weekdays from 8 am to 4 pm, issues permits. A building permit is required to construct, enlarge, alter, repair or demolish, or to change a building's use. The fee is $20 up to $3,000 of work, then $2.50 per $1,000 above that up to $500,000. All fences need a permit, and an accessory structure under 200 square feet falls under a no-fee permit. A certificate of occupancy costs $3 after a final inspection.

Converting a house to a short-term rental counts as a change of use. It needs inspections and a $45 Short Term Rental Permit. If you are selling a house that someone else operates that way, ask for the permit paperwork. No permit is needed just to sell, but close out any open permit work before you list.

sections.h2: Selling a rental or a house with tenants
sections.html:
Because renters fill most of the housing here, many sellers own a rental. Tell the buyer's side early whether the house is occupied, when the lease ends and whether the tenant pays on time. Hand over the lease and the deposit records, and ask the closing agent to credit the deposit at the table. A house that has been a short-term rental should come with its permit paperwork, since the city permit is tied to the operator and not the property.

If a vacant rental needs work between leases, a direct cash buyer may suit you better than a listing, because the buyer does not need the house to pass a lender's appraisal and you avoid carrying another month of costs while it sits empty.

1. Confirm which school district and tax rate apply to the address.
  2. Check the sheriff's bill and the city bill, and ask the clerk about any earlier year.
  3. Gather permit papers for any recent work and rental permits if relevant.
  4. Get a mortgage payoff letter close to the planned closing date.
  5. Agree in the contract who pays the year's tax and who covers repairs.

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so repairs and a lien paid from proceeds do not hold up the sale the way they can with a lender. Whichever route you choose, keep copies of the bills, payoff letters and permits in one folder, and ask the closing agent for a settlement statement ahead of time so every charge makes sense before you sign.

faqs.q: What is the current population of Bowling Green, KY?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 78,505 residents, up from 72,294 counted in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: What is the typical home value in Bowling Green?
faqs.a: The median owner-occupied value is $241,900. Only 36.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Is Bowling Green property tax higher inside the city?
faqs.a: Yes. The total real estate rate is 1.3625 per $100 for city proper, 1.0455 for the annex and 0.8425 outside city limits.

faqs.q: Which office handles a delinquent Bowling Green tax bill?
faqs.a: The Warren County Clerk, at (270) 842-9416, for a payoff. The County Attorney at (270) 782-2760 sets up payment plans.

faqs.q: Is a city permit required to list a Bowling Green house?
faqs.a: No permit is needed to sell, but the city requires them for building work and for converting a house to a short-term rental. Close out any open permit work before you list.
